exposure: mode of delivery (vacuum extraction vs. spontaneous vaginal birth vs. emergency cesarean section)
cohort: 1,509,589 term singleton children in Sweden planned for vaginal birth (January 1, 1999 to December 31, 2017)
finding: In this nationwide cohort study, children born after successful VE had no increased risk of ND, CP, or epilepsy compared with those delivered by ECS, but there was an increased risk of ND among those born by failed VE.
mod_finding: Children born after successful VE had no increased risk of ND, CP, or epilepsy compared with those delivered by ECS, but there was an increased risk of ND among those born by failed VE.
